title: How FanDuel is bringing betting into the social conversation
body_markdown:
##### **Built around behaviour**


Perhaps the most interesting aspect of the partnership is that sports betting was already part of the conversation. According to Real's research, which has been published by[FanDuel](https://fanduel.com/about/news/real-sports-partner-with-fanduel) , around 75% of their users who commented on player performances had previously discussed sports betting. Users have also actively requested live odds and betting-related information within the platform. Rather than introducing an entirely new behavior, the partnership responds to one that already existed.


From a consumer perspective, that matters. Fans were already discussing bets and looking for betting context. The integration simply brings that information closer to the moments where those conversations are already happening.


The rise of platforms like Real highlights another broader trend in sports consumption – data is increasingly becoming content in its own right. Fans do not just consume sports through broadcasts. They follow player performance metrics, live statistics, highlights, commentary and social reactions alongside the action.


Research from[WSC Sports](https://wsc-sports.com/blog/reports/the-2025-2026-generational-fan-study/) found that 62% of sports fans have discovered a new team, player or league through short-form video content, underlining how sports discovery is increasingly happening beyond traditional channels. Odds can play a similar role. They provide another layer of context around what is happening during a game and can spark discussion, debate and interaction among fans following the action in real time.
